$comment: INIT-5 deployment registry. ADR-011 §3: no upgradeable proxy — a logic change is a NEW deployment,
so this file carries ONE ENTRY PER VERSION and old entries are never edited or deleted (v1 receipts
stay claimable and must stay readable after v2 goes live — ADR-011 'Consequences').
RESOLUTION RULE: this file is a CATALOG, not a chronological log. Besides the deployments we
actually operate it also carries synthetic per-fund read-API fixtures (the TEST-* entries), which
the frontend and the read-API fold project from DB-faked events with no contract behind them.
Entries are therefore NOT ordered by recency, and array position must never be read as recency.
Resolve an entry by `deployedAt` (newest wins), or pin one explicitly. Both consumers do this:
services  RegistryService.activeDeployment() -- REX_VERSION if pinned, else newest deployedAt
@rex/ops  readDeployment()                   -- newest deployedAt (same comparator, verbatim)
Keep the two in sync: ops resolved by array position until 2026-09-04, which silently pointed
`ops read` / `ops tx --env sepolia` at TEST-PORTFOLIO-1.0.0 (0xde00...0006, no code on chain)
instead of the live SC10-1.0.0.
So: an entry that is NOT meant to be operated must carry a deliberately ancient `deployedAt` --
the convention the TEST-* fixtures established with 2026-01-01. That, plus REX_VERSION pinning,
is what keeps them inert.
A throwaway QA/demo instance is better recorded OUTSIDE this file, under config/deploy/ (see
config/deploy/tester-instance.json, the 2026-09-01 QA instance -- release 1.0.1 bytecode, but
stalenessWindow = type(uint256).max, which @rex/ops cannot even represent as a JS number). Such an
instance is still valid evidence that a version works on testnet; it is just not a registry entry.
SCOPE RULE: this schema records only what the contracts ACTUALLY implement today. It deliberately
does NOT carry fields for surfaces that exist as interface declarations only — adding them would
invite a consumer to depend on a call that reverts. Add a field in the same PR that implements it.
Deployables today — four (see DeploymentEntry in services/src/config/deployments.types.ts):
home.rexPrimary        contracts/src/REXPrimary.sol:19  `is ERC1155, BridgeAdapter, IREXSubscribe`
home.navOracleConsumer contracts/src/NavOracleConsumer.sol:13 `is Ownable, ReentrancyGuard, IMessageRecipient`
home.epochSchedule     contracts/src/EpochSchedule.sol `is IEpochSchedule` (SC11 / ADR-025):
immutable, stateless epoch calendar. Optional + nullable, absent on any
entry recorded before SC11.
fund.pruvExecutor      contracts/src/PruvExecutor.sol:23 `is BridgeAdapter, IERC1155Receiver, IPruvExecutor`
`BridgeAdapter` is `abstract` (contracts/src/BridgeAdapter.sol:21) and inherited by both — it is NOT
deployed standalone and gets no address.
constructorArgs mirror the real constructors verbatim, so a deploy is reproducible and verifiable:
REXPrimary        usdc · mailbox · usdcRoute · wrwaRoute · pruvDomain · minSub
· launchpadStart · launchpadPeriod · launchpadMinimum · cancelFeeBps
· feeRecipient · sc3Params { minRedeem · redeemCancelFeeBps · maxSubWait
· maxRedeemPerEpoch · maxRedeemWait · redemptionFeeBps
· redeemFulfillTimeout · windDownWindow } — SC3Params minus `navOracle`
and (SC11+) `schedule`, whose resolved addresses are `home.navOracleConsumer`
/ `home.epochSchedule` above, not repeated here. SC11 also dropped `keeper`
(ADR-025) — optional going forward, present only on pre-SC11 entries.
PruvExecutor       mailbox · wrwaRoute · homeDomain · rwaToken · usdc · usdcRoute
· subFulfillTimeout · executorSlippageBps · redeemFulfillTimeout (SC8a added
the last 4; pre-SC8a entries recorded only the first 5).
NavOracleConsumer  mailbox · reporterDomain · stalenessWindow · maxNavMoveBps (SC8a: recorded
here now that a write reads this contract's real deploy args back).
The launchpad block arrived with SC2 (2026-07-31). It is IMMUTABLE and there is no startLaunchpad()
call — the window is defined entirely by these values (ADR-007: launchpad is time-based, closing is
permissionless), so a wrong value is only fixable by redeploying (ADR-011). cancelFeeBps is bounded
by feeCapBps (init 200, admin-settable via setFeeCap under CONFIG_TIMELOCK, no hard ceiling — ADR-007 A1); the rate is snapshotted at request time.
`version` is now READ FROM ON-CHAIN `VERSION()` (SC6) AND ASSERTED: ADR-011 §3 wanted
`string public constant VERSION`, and REXPrimary.sol now exposes exactly that. A write must read
it back and assert it matches before recording this entry — it is no longer purely
registry-assigned, as it was pre-SC6.
navOracleConsumer was REMOVED on 2026-07-29 because no such contract existed, and is BACK as of
SC3 (2026-08-05) because it now does: NavOracleConsumer.sol is deployed on the home chain, emits
NavUpdated, and REXPrimary reads it via nav() instead of the old hardcoded 1e18. It is OPTIONAL and
NULLABLE in the schema — an entry written before SC3 has no such key, and the home crawler then
watches REXPrimary alone rather than filtering on a guessed address. Its own constructor args
(mailbox / reporterDomain / stalenessWindow / maxNavMoveBps) are now recorded at
constructorArgs.navOracleConsumer (added SC8a; optional, absent on pre-SC8a entries). That is
independent of NAV_STALENESS_SECONDS in .env, which is what /nav reports against today and MUST
still be kept equal to the deployed stalenessWindow() by hand — nothing yet cross-checks the two.
fund.navReporter (contracts/src/NavReporter.sol) is the PRUV NAV feed, built by SC9 (Core-1) and
deployed + recorded at SC8d P4. It reads RWAConversion.value() and dispatches it to
home.navOracleConsumer (ADR-004 A1). OPTIONAL and NULLABLE — absent on any pre-SC9 entry (the live
SC6-1.0.0 entry has no such key yet); constructorArgs.navReporter mirrors its real constructor
(mailbox / homeDomain / consumer / source / heartbeat). BE5 (AT-70 §2) reads this address to operate the relay.
NOT in this schema, and why (do not add speculatively):
launchpad params (start/period/minimum/cancelFeeBps/feeRecipient) — the SC2 design describes them
as immutable constructor args, but SC2 is unmerged (branch feat/SC2-launchpad carries design +
plan docs only) and the live constructor takes none of them.
fee config — no fee logic is built; the constructor takes no fee parameter.
redeem addresses/params — IREXRedeem is a frozen DECLARATION only, inherited at SC5
(shared/src/IREXPrimary.sol:26-28).
Empty until a testnet deploy runs. Nothing is deployed yet — gate G2 is open, SC1 has never run on
testnet (docs/planning/story-list.md:248).
